pages.hook: In the USA, birthdays are a big deal, but asking an adult “How old are you?” can feel private. Learn when the question is polite.

mythfact.s: In English, you say “I have 30 years”.
mythfact.why: English uses be: “I’m 30.”

mythfact.s: In the USA, the legal drinking age is 21 in all states.
mythfact.why: A national law pushes every state to set 21 as the age to buy alcohol, with a few narrow exceptions.

mythfact.s: Houston is where NASA’s mission control for human spaceflight is.
mythfact.why: The Johnson Space Center is in Houston. “Houston, we’ve had a problem” is from Apollo 13.

mythfact.s: Asking a stranger her age is always polite.
mythfact.why: Many adults think it is private. With children and friends, it is fine.

mythfact.s: People often sing “Happy Birthday to You” with a cake.
mythfact.why: The song and a cake with candles are a US tradition.

decode.why: “Happy 30th Birthday” means he is turning thirty.

lines: Come to the party on June 12.
Bring a gift. Cake and music!

decode.why: Mia is turning 15, so it is her birthday.

compare.br: In Brazil, people sing “Parabéns pra você” and the first piece of cake is often given to someone special.
compare.us: In the USA, people sing “Happy Birthday to You”, the person blows out the candles and makes a wish.
compare.tip: Say “I’m thirty”, not “I have thirty”. Be, not have.
compare.ask: How old are you? When is your birthday? Answer in English.

quiz.q: How do you say your age?
Your friend’s birthday is tomorrow. You say…
quiz.why: Happy early birthday is natural before the day.

pages.polite: Say **“Happy birthday!”** with a smile, and add **“Many happy returns!”**, which sounds more British. In the USA, a simple wish is perfect.

Reading quest — Thirty, thirty-one and a mermaid · part 1
text: Today is my friend Omar’s birthday. He lives in Houston, Texas. “**I’m twenty-five!**” he said last year. This year, he is **thirty**. “**Happy birthday!**” I said.

My birthday is in June, so I am turning **thirty-one**. “**How old are you?**” Omar asked me. “**I’m thirty. My birthday is in June**,” I said. He said, “**Happy early birthday!**” It was funny, because it was still May.
Omar has a young sister. “**How old is** your sister?” I asked. “**She’s fifteen**,” he said. “She is young!” We looked at her photo. She **looks like** her mother.

pages.title: Reading quest — Thirty, thirty-one and a mermaid · part 2
text: At the party, we ate a big cake and sang. Omar blew out the candles and made a wish. Houston is a big city and the home of NASA, so Omar said, “My wish is to go to space!”

On the way home, I thought of an old story. In 1837, the Danish writer Hans Christian Andersen wrote “The Little Mermaid”. The mermaid is **fifteen** in the story. She lives in the sea and dreams of the human world. In Copenhagen, there is a small statue of her by the water. Fifteen is young, but she has a big dream. I think a birthday is a good day to make one.
